values.src: Sky playing 0.2.122 (brief 067 item 6: "Players move pretty slowly"); Motive briefs/067/motive.md §1

Legs shorten by 22 %: the service lane to the getaway bay (65.0 m) 46.4 s -> 36.1 s. Only the cell reads it after the split (M067-B1): an operative's walk and carry of Vale or a body (the Enforcer), and every preview of the cell's walk (the approach card, the move quote, the fire walk-in, the carry sight, the cancel's time left). Measured (results/ens-*.tsv, cand-final-w180.txt): at 1.6 every plan that wins today still wins as composed (start delays 0-3 s 7/7, each operative 0-2 s 8/8); at 1.8 board and go gets easier (route-a-pressure-board 0/8 -> 6/8, route-g-kill-board 0/8 -> 8/8 with the hold at (2000, -6500)) and five fight plans need re-composing (Waymark, 'recompose' below); with them the mission check holds MC-1 (A, B, G), MC-2, MC-5, MC-6 (122.6 s), MC-10, MC-11, MC-12 and fails only MC-7 on careless-g-disable. Fallback if Sky wants no plan changes: 160 (run 320, untrained carry 80), every plan holds unchanged.

rules.key: the walk split (cell.speed is the cell's; people-walk-cm-s the city's)
rules.value: The cell walks at cell.speed (1.8 m/s); everyone the engine walks itself walks at people-walk-cm-s (1.4 m/s): the summoned partner, reporters and tellers walking to a phone, a witness walking to a body, the crowd walking back from shelter. The rounds bake's paceCmPerS is checked against people-walk-cm-s. Runs keep their own paces (cell.runSpeed for the cell, crowd.run for a fleeing person, rivals-follow-cm-s for the posted three).
rules.reason: Without the split a faster cell walks the city faster too: Inez's call window would shrink (58 s -> 45 s each way), reports would land sooner and the rounds file would need a rebake. The probe's PROBE_OPWALK is this split (the cell's pace only).
rules.checks: PACE-SPLIT: an operative's 18 m walk takes 10.0 s; route A's call logs 'walks over to her (58 s)' as on 0.33.1; a knockout's reporter lands its report at the same tick as on 0.33.1; handover.rounds.json loads unchanged.

rules.value: A run is seen and suspicious, never an Alert on its own. A security watcher that keeps an attention clock (a live camera, the door guard not the cell's ally, the patrol, the response's officers and robots), with a running operative in its sight (its sight for the clock: the live cone, and for a person also attention.near), lifts its clock on that operative to the band's noticed mark at the run's first tick in its sight, and adds 1 s a second while the run stays in its sight, as standing still does; the stages, the wary mark and the report are attention's own (a report lands as a loiterer's: a found fault, Alert to at least alert-inquiry, no Trail, a sighting, the dial's Alert-1 response). Out of its sight, or walking, the clock drains as today. A run that is loud, under fire, or at Alert 2 and above (cell.run's free cases) adds nothing. Security staff who keep no clock (the shift guards on the street, StaffSees) and anyone in witness range who would remember a run today still remember it (memory saw-runner: a sighting, no T, no Alert, no Standing); the guard who saw a runner still no longer fights at your side. From Alert 2 ordinary people who see a run in their cone remember the face, as built (Sky's 054 call, kept). run.seen stays in the log as the sighting, without 'a found fault'.
rules.reason: Readable: the first tick a watcher sees a run, its cue shows noticed (the lens, the face, the head), so the player learns that running is seen without an Alert to learn it from. Proportional: one pass costs the noticed cue; a run held in sight makes the watcher wary after (wary - noticed) s (12 s at Heat 0, 9 s infamous) and reports it after (report - noticed) s (37 s at Heat 0, 15 s infamous). Measured (results/run-camera.txt): the Scout running 16 legs across the entrance camera's view: today Alert 1 at the first sight (0:20.9); with the rule noticed at 0:16.3, wary at 0:28.2, reported 0:53.2, landed 0:57.6 (Alert 1). No quiet reference route gains a report (MC-12 13/13 at every candidate).
rules.checks: RUN-NOTICED: the run-camera script (results/run-camera.txt) logs attention.noticed on the run's first tick in sight and no Alert; wary 12.0 s of run in sight later (Heat 0); reported 37 s later; on landing Alert 1. RUN-NOT-ALERT: route A ends at Alert 0 (0.33.1: 1); its run.seen lines stay. RUN-FREE: at Alert 2 a run moves no clock.

rules.value: Confirmed as the rule [S]: a Drive under way is no cancel; the car drives on to the stand it was given and stops only at a stand. Its riders are busy until it stands (any order refused agent-busy, a cancel car-driving), so nobody steps out of a moving car. Go during a Drive is taken and is a withdrawal: a Drive never carries Vale (drive-fight: refused once the final fight has started).
rules.reason: A stand is the only place the car's rules exist (its exit lane, ambush spots, police stands, cover); a car stopped on the road would be a stand with none of them (unknown = reject). The order shows its price before commit (the stand and its seconds: 28.4 s from the square to the service drive), and the HUD shows the stand and the seconds left while it drives, so the commitment is read before it is made. A re-target mid-drive (turn back) is not worth its rules: readable > rich.
rules.gdd: §06 Drive: add 'A Drive under way runs to its stand: it can't be stopped, and nobody gets out until the car stands.'

rules.value: Accepted as Keel built them [S]: a walker's centre keeps 50 cm off a standing car's body (473 x 182 cm on its heading); 'at the car' (Board, and a rival reaching Vale in the getaway car) is within 1 m of the body. The 6 m guard ring of 'rivals reach Vale' (cell.reach) stays measured from the car's point.
rules.reason: 50 cm is one walk cell, so the first free ring round a standing car is always 'at it' (the band 50-100 cm is one full cell wide) and a string-pulled walk still passes the body about a shoulder clear: Sky's 'walking through cars' is gone and no side of a car loses its Board. The building clearance (65 cm, plan body.r) would leave a 35 cm band, narrower than a cell, with gaps where no free cell is at the car. The 1 m reach covers about 8.9 m2 outside the clearance against the 7 m2 the old 1.5 m circle round the centre held (Keel's reason), so 'rivals reach Vale' is no easier. Every number in this file is measured on 0.33.1, so with these two values.
rules.gdd: §06 Board: 'by any op within 1 m of the car's body'; rivals reach Vale: 'a rival within 1 m of the car's body'.

rules.key: the end of a fight the cell can no longer fight (BAL-YARD-AT-WILL: the Enforcer downed in the car with Vale at 7:30.0, the run idle to 8:30)
rules.value: (a) Hiding in a held car loses [S]: in the safe fight, with Vale in the getaway car and no operative standing outside it (every one down, or every standing one in the car), the rivals up and not broken, the blocker excepted (he keeps his lane), walk to the car, firing as they walk; the first within car-reach of its body takes Vale (fail rivals-reach-vale, as today). An operative standing outside again stops it: they go back to cover (how they walk, there and back, is Pulse's, as the press for the Vale holder; the probe models the walk there only). (b) The cell down [S]: once every operative is down (in the car or not), the mission fails at once (fail cell-down: 'The whole cell is down'), the fail camera on the last to fall. (c) Go needs a driver [S]: Go is taken only with a standing operative in the car; with only the downed aboard it is refused (car-no-driver: 'nobody aboard can drive'); any standing operative may still give it, from anywhere, once one is aboard. No new timer: the safe fight still ends by the cell's acts, (a), (b), Withdraw, or (loud) the seal.
rules.reason: GDD §06 makes the Enforcer 'any op' once Vale is in the car and says hiding in a held car loses; the engine had no way to lose that way: the rivals hold cover, the downed Enforcer can't be shot dead, the Tech in the car is no foe under ai.intent.final agent, and Go stays refused (car-held: rival-3). Measured on the probe (results/yard-at-will-0.33.1.txt, yard-at-will-k3.txt): 0.33.1 ends None at 8:30.0 (the script's end); with (a)-(c) the Scout falls at 7:38.3, rival-1 and rival-2 go for the car at 7:38.4 and rival-1 reaches it at 7:46.5: rivals-reach-vale. On every script of HEAD's route set and of the candidate set, (a)-(c) move no outcome; route-a-board's final hash moves at its Go tick (2675), where the three's boards land, the rivals' walk starts and Go is taken in one tick (read the condition after the tick's orders, and no hash moves).
rules.checks: BAL-YARD-AT-WILL: fails rivals-reach-vale (probe 7:46.5), the rivals' walk logged when the last operative outside goes down (7:38.3). K3-CELL-DOWN: every operative down with Vale in the car: fail cell-down that tick. K3-DRIVER: Go with only the downed Enforcer and Vale aboard is refused car-no-driver; the Scout boards (1 s) and Go is taken. Text for Fable: cell-down (fail), car-no-driver (refusal), the rivals' walk to the car (log).

rules.key: loud Trail 12 (ai.intent.final agent) against 14 (every), FinalIntent F15_ROUTES
rules.value: Both are §06's rule, applied the same way. The 2 T between them is one down: under every, rival-1 falls at 4:18.3 (+2 T down:rival-1) before the Enforcer does; under agent the hostiles do not fire on the operatives who did nothing, the fight runs differently and rival-1 is still up at 4:26.4. The ledger is otherwise identical: loop 1, reroute 1, the guard 2 + 2 + 2, rival-1 2 + 2. The game's number is agent's (the rulebook's, provisional, Sky 'sounds right'): 12 on the failing c037 loud scripts. The re-composed loud (loud-x4, the reference loud win) costs 27 T under both. Keel's test shape (Trail under agent <= under every) is the right one.
rules.reason: The mismatch is in the GDD text, not between the two runs: §06 'cost' says +2 T per person hit and +2 T if they go down, 'a dropped guard = 4 T'; the rulebook also charges gunfire-trail +2 T once per shooting (the first shot at each target, hit or miss: Motive's fights addendum Q1, Sky-approved 2026-10-15), so the engine's dropped guard is 6 T (gunfire:guard 2, hit:guard 2, down:guard 2).
rules.gdd: §06 cost: '+2 T once per shooting (the first shot at each target, hit or miss), +2 T per person hit (once), +2 T more if they go down (a dropped guard = 6 T)'; §02 Trail: 'people shot at or hit by gunfire'.
